# Medical Interview (XVII)

On May 14, 2024, the investigator conducted a comprehensive medical interview with SUBJECT at the DCSA field office in Arlington, Virginia. The interview was conducted as part of the personnel security investigation and focused on SUBJECT's medical history, mental health treatment, and current health status. SUBJECT appeared cooperative and forthcoming throughout the interview, demonstrating willingness to discuss sensitive medical matters and providing detailed responses to all inquiries.

SUBJECT reported no significant childhood illnesses or hospitalizations. SUBJECT stated that routine vaccinations were completed according to standard schedules and that no chronic medical conditions exist at present. SUBJECT denied current use of prescription medications and reported no known allergies to medications or environmental substances. SUBJECT indicated that annual physical examinations have been maintained regularly, with the most recent examination conducted in March 2024 by Dr. Patricia Chen, MD, at Fairfax Medical Associates in Fairfax, Virginia.

Regarding mental health history, SUBJECT disclosed a period of significant psychological distress during 2016-2021, which SUBJECT attributed to marital difficulties and occupational stress. SUBJECT stated that during this period, alcohol consumption escalated as a coping mechanism, and that SUBJECT ultimately sought professional intervention following two driving under the influence (DUI) arrests in 2019 and 2021. SUBJECT described this period as a critical turning point and indicated that the experience prompted comprehensive reassessment of personal priorities and coping strategies.

SUBJECT reported voluntary enrollment in a residential treatment program at Serenity Springs Treatment Center in Asheville, North Carolina, from January 2022 through March 2022. SUBJECT stated that the program provided a 60-day intensive treatment curriculum addressing underlying psychological factors contributing to alcohol use disorder. SUBJECT identified the treatment provider as Dr. Michael Rothstein, PhD, Clinical Director of Serenity Springs, and stated that the program included individual psychotherapy, group counseling, family therapy sessions, and structured educational components addressing addiction recovery and relapse prevention. SUBJECT noted that the program operated on an abstinence-based model and included peer support components.

SUBJECT reported that upon completion of the residential program in March 2022, participation in Alcoholics Anonymous (AA) began and has continued to present. SUBJECT stated that AA meetings are attended on a regular basis, typically two to three times per week, and that a sponsor relationship has been established and maintained. SUBJECT identified the AA sponsor as Robert Downey, a professional colleague in the construction industry, and indicated that contact with the sponsor occurs on a weekly basis minimum. SUBJECT stated that the support group participation has been instrumental in maintaining sobriety and that no relapse incidents have occurred since program completion.

When asked about current mental health status, SUBJECT reported feeling substantially improved compared to the 2016-2021 period. SUBJECT stated that ongoing counseling or psychotherapy is not currently being pursued, but that the AA sponsor relationship and group participation provide adequate psychological support. SUBJECT acknowledged that the court-ordered treatment program requirement has been fully satisfied and that continued participation in AA is entirely voluntary. SUBJECT demonstrated insight into the previous problematic behaviors and articulated understanding of the factors that contributed to the alcohol-related incidents.

SUBJECT reported that family relationships have improved substantially since achieving sobriety. SUBJECT stated that marital reconciliation efforts have progressed positively and that communication with adult children has normalized. SUBJECT indicated that these improved relationships have reinforced motivation to maintain abstinence and that family support has been a significant factor in sustained recovery. SUBJECT denied any current depressive symptoms, anxiety disorders, or suicidal ideation. SUBJECT reported sleep patterns have normalized and that overall sense of well-being has improved markedly.

Regarding employment and occupational functioning, SUBJECT reported that work performance has remained stable and that no workplace incidents or disciplinary actions have occurred since the DUI arrests. SUBJECT stated that supervisors and colleagues have been generally supportive and that job responsibilities have not been affected by the previous alcohol-related issues. SUBJECT indicated that financial stability has been maintained and that no significant financial stressors currently exist. SUBJECT denied any current involvement with law enforcement or pending legal matters.

SUBJECT was asked directly about current alcohol consumption patterns. SUBJECT stated unequivocally that complete abstinence has been maintained since February 2022 and that no alcoholic beverages have been consumed since that date. SUBJECT acknowledged that this represents more than two years of continuous sobriety and expressed commitment to maintaining abstinence indefinitely. SUBJECT stated that the previous pattern of alcohol use is inconsistent with current values and priorities, and that the consequences of the DUI arrests served as a powerful deterrent against future alcohol consumption.

The investigator noted that SUBJECT's account of the treatment experience and recovery process was consistent with information previously obtained from Serenity Springs Treatment Center records and from the AA sponsor interview. SUBJECT's presentation during the medical interview was coherent, organized, and reflective, with appropriate emotional tone and no indicators of active mental health disturbance. SUBJECT demonstrated appropriate insight into previous behavioral patterns and articulated realistic understanding of ongoing recovery requirements.

Following the medical interview, the investigator initiated contact with Dr. Patricia Chen, MD, at Fairfax Medical Associates to verify SUBJECT's reported medical history and current health status. Dr. Chen confirmed that SUBJECT has been a patient at the clinic since 2018 and that annual physical examinations have been maintained. Dr. Chen reported no significant acute medical conditions, no chronic disease states, and no current prescription medications. Dr. Chen indicated that SUBJECT's health status is generally good and that no medical concerns exist that would affect occupational functioning or security clearance eligibility.

Authorization for release of medical records from Serenity Springs Treatment Center was obtained from SUBJECT, and records were subsequently requested. Records confirmed that SUBJECT was enrolled in the residential treatment program from January 15, 2022, through March 18, 2022. Treatment records documented a diagnosis of Alcohol Use Disorder, moderate severity, with contributing factors identified as marital stress, occupational pressure, and inadequate coping mechanisms. Treatment records indicated that SUBJECT responded well to the therapeutic interventions and demonstrated high engagement with all program components. Clinical notes documented SUBJECT's expressed commitment to abstinence and active participation in peer support activities during the treatment episode.

Discharge summary from Serenity Springs Treatment Center, dated March 18, 2022, documented successful completion of the treatment program with a prognosis of good recovery potential contingent upon continued engagement with support group activities and maintenance of abstinence. The discharge summary recommended ongoing participation in AA or similar peer support groups and noted that SUBJECT had already established initial contact with AA prior to discharge. Dr. Michael Rothstein, Clinical Director, signed the discharge summary and noted in clinical observations that SUBJECT demonstrated mature insight into the addiction process and expressed realistic commitment to long-term recovery.

On April 18, 2024, the investigator conducted an in-person interview with Ragnar Lothbrok, spouse of SUBJECT, at the couple's residence located at 4782 Oakmont Drive, Arlington, Virginia 22207. Mr. Lothbrok was cooperative and forthcoming throughout the interview, which lasted approximately ninety minutes. He appeared well-organized and provided documentation to support statements made during the conversation.

Mr. Lothbrok reported that he was born on July 14, 1985, in Minneapolis, Minnesota, and is a natural-born United States citizen. He provided a copy of his birth certificate issued by Hennepin County, Minnesota, which was reviewed and verified by the investigator. Mr. Lothbrok holds a current U.S. passport (No. 847291056) issued on March 3, 2021, and valid through March 2, 2031. He reported no dual citizenship or allegiance to any foreign power.

Regarding his professional background, Mr. Lothbrok stated that he has been employed as a Senior Systems Architect with Northpoint Technology Solutions, located in Reston, Virginia, since January 2019. He provided copies of his employment offer letter and recent performance evaluations, which were reviewed. Mr. Lothbrok reported that his current annual salary is approximately $142,000. Prior to this position, he worked as a Network Administrator for Cascade IT Consulting in Seattle, Washington, from June 2015 to December 2018. Mr. Lothbrok noted that he left that position due to a relocation to the Washington, D.C. area to be closer to SUBJECT's employment.

When asked about his educational background, Mr. Lothbrok reported that he earned a Bachelor of Science degree in Computer Science from the University of Washington in Seattle in 2007. He provided a diploma and official transcript, both of which were verified through the university's registrar office. Mr. Lothbrok stated that he has not pursued any graduate-level education but has completed several professional certifications in network security and cloud infrastructure management through online platforms.

Mr. Lothbrok reported that he and SUBJECT were married on June 22, 2018, in Arlington, Virginia. He stated that the couple has one biological child together, Ivar Lothbrok, born November 3, 2018. Mr. Lothbrok confirmed that he has no children from previous relationships. Marriage records were subsequently verified through Arlington County Circuit Court. Mr. Lothbrok described his relationship with SUBJECT as stable and supportive, noting that they maintain regular communication regarding household and family matters.

When questioned regarding foreign contacts and travel, Mr. Lothbrok reported limited international activity. He stated that he has traveled to Canada on three occasions for personal leisure (2016, 2019, and 2022), visiting Vancouver and Whistler. He also reported a single trip to Mexico in 2017 with friends to Cancun for a week-long vacation. Mr. Lothbrok stated that he has no family residing outside the United States and no ongoing business interests abroad. He reported no contact with foreign nationals, with the exception of occasional professional interactions with international clients of Northpoint Technology Solutions, which he characterized as routine business communication via email and video conference.

Regarding financial matters, Mr. Lothbrok reported that he and SUBJECT maintain joint checking and savings accounts with First National Bank of Arlington. He stated that the couple's combined household income is approximately $185,000 annually. When asked about any financial difficulties, Mr. Lothbrok initially stated that finances were stable; however, upon further inquiry, he disclosed that the couple had experienced some cash flow challenges in late 2023 due to unexpected home repairs and medical expenses related to their son's dental work. Mr. Lothbrok noted that they had carried a credit card balance of approximately $8,000 during that period but had since reduced it to $2,100 as of the interview date. He provided recent credit card statements and bank records to support this account. Records review confirmed the general accuracy of Mr. Lothbrok's financial reporting, though the investigator noted that the couple's credit report reflected a 60-day late payment on a credit card account in November 2023, which Mr. Lothbrok attributed to a processing error that was subsequently resolved.

Mr. Lothbrok reported that he is not a member of any foreign organizations or political groups. He stated that he votes regularly in U.S. elections and has no allegiance to any foreign government or ideology. He confirmed that he has never been arrested, charged with any crime, or involved in any legal proceedings. Background records review confirmed the absence of any criminal history associated with Mr. Lothbrok in Virginia, Washington, or federal databases.

When asked about his awareness of SUBJECT's work and security responsibilities, Mr. Lothbrok stated that he understands SUBJECT works for a federal agency in a position involving sensitive information. He reported that SUBJECT has briefed him on the importance of operational security and that they maintain appropriate safeguards regarding classified or sensitive materials in their home. Mr. Lothbrok stated that he does not have access to any of SUBJECT's work materials and that SUBJECT does not discuss the specifics of her employment with him. He appeared to understand the security implications of SUBJECT's position and expressed commitment to supporting SUBJECT's compliance with security protocols.

Mr. Lothbrok reported regular social contact with friends and colleagues but stated that his social circle is limited to the Arlington area. He named several coworkers and neighbors as acquaintances but reported no close friendships outside of his relationship with SUBJECT and their immediate family. When asked about substance use, Mr. Lothbrok reported occasional alcohol consumption, typically limited to social gatherings or weekend dinners. He stated that he does not use tobacco products and has never used illegal drugs. He reported no mental health treatment or counseling.

In conclusion, Mr. Lothbrok presented as a stable, employed individual with no apparent security concerns. His background is consistent with what he reported, his financial situation, while showing minor recent stress, appears manageable, and he demonstrated appropriate awareness of the security implications of SUBJECT's employment. Mr. Lothbrok expressed full support for SUBJECT's federal service and stated his willingness to cooperate with any future security inquiries.

On April 22, 2024, the investigator contacted Glenn MNU Avery, Manager of Human Resources at Northpoint Technology Solutions, located at 11600 Sunrise Valley Drive, Reston, Virginia 20191, to verify Mr. Lothbrok's employment and obtain information regarding his professional conduct and reliability. Mr. Avery confirmed that Mr. Lothbrok has been employed as a Senior Systems Architect since January 15, 2019, and remains in active employment with the company. Mr. Avery stated that Mr. Lothbrok's current annual salary is $142,500, consistent with Mr. Lothbrok's reported figure.

The investigator noted that the couple maintains a modest emergency savings account of approximately $12,000, which Mr. Lothbrok indicated was intentionally maintained for unexpected expenses.

On May 6, 2024, the investigator conducted comprehensive criminal background checks for Mr. Lothbrok through the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) National Crime Information Center (NCIC), the Virginia State Police, the Washington State Patrol, and the Minnesota Bureau of Criminal Apprehension. Records confirmed that Mr. Lothbrok has no criminal history, arrests, charges, or convictions in any jurisdiction. Additionally, a search of the National Sex Offender Public Website (NSOPW) returned no results associated with Mr. Lothbrok.

The investigator also reviewed court records from Arlington County Circuit Court, Hennepin County District Court (Minnesota), and King County Superior Court (Washington) to verify the absence of any civil litigation, protective orders, or other legal proceedings involving Mr. Lothbrok. No such records were identified. Records confirmed that Mr. Lothbrok's marriage to SUBJECT is documented in Arlington County records and remains valid and in good standing.

On May 10, 2024, the investigator reviewed Mr. Lothbrok's U.S. passport records and obtained travel history through the Department of State Passport Services. Passport records confirmed that Mr. Lothbrok holds a valid U.S. passport (No. 847291056) issued on March 3, 2021, and valid through March 2, 2031. Travel history review confirmed Mr. Lothbrok's reported international travel: three trips to Canada (Vancouver area) in July 2016, August 2019, and June 2022, and one trip to Mexico (Cancun) in March 2017. All travel was consistent with personal leisure tourism, and entry and exit records were consistent with Mr. Lothbrok's reported dates and destinations.

The investigator inquired with Mr. Lothbrok regarding any foreign contacts or relationships. Mr. Lothbrok confirmed that he has no family members residing outside the United States and no ongoing personal relationships with foreign nationals. He stated that his professional interactions with international contacts are limited to routine business communications with clients of Northpoint Technology Solutions and are conducted in English via email and video conference. Mr. Lothbrok provided examples of such contacts, which the investigator verified as legitimate business communications. No derogatory information regarding foreign contacts was identified.

The investigation of Mr. Ragnar Lothbrok, spouse of SUBJECT, revealed a stable individual with appropriate background, employment, and financial circumstances. Mr. Lothbrok is a natural-born U.S. citizen with no foreign allegiances or concerning foreign contacts. His employment history is consistent and satisfactory, with positive references from his current employer. His financial situation, while showing minor stress in late 2023, is generally stable and manageable, with the couple demonstrating financial responsibility through timely resolution of delinquencies.

Mr. Lothbrok's background check revealed no criminal history, no civil litigation of concern, and no substance abuse or mental health issues of significance. His international travel is limited and consistent with personal tourism. Mr. Lothbrok demonstrated appropriate awareness of security protocols related to SUBJECT's employment and expressed commitment to supporting SUBJECT's compliance with federal security requirements. Neighbor references characterized him as a responsible and courteous member of the community.

Based on the totality of the investigation, Mr. Lothbrok presents no apparent security concerns and appears to be a suitable spouse for an individual seeking a position of public trust with the federal government. No derogatory information was identified that would warrant further investigation or security concern.

# Unemployment (VIII)

SUBJECT reported continuous employment in the agricultural sector spanning approximately fifteen years, with no significant periods of unemployment. The investigator reviewed SUBJECT's employment record as follows: Field Technician at Pinnacle Agricultural Services, Inc., Syracuse, New York, from June 1, 2009, to July 14, 2011; Agricultural Inspector with the New York Department of Agriculture and Markets, Rochester, New York, from July 15, 2011, to February 28, 2015; and Agriculture Specialist with U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), Buffalo, New York, from March 1, 2015, to present. SUBJECT's current employment with CBP remains ongoing at the time of this investigation.

The investigator conducted a detailed review of the transition periods between SUBJECT's positions to identify any gaps in employment or periods of unemployment. Between SUBJECT's departure from Pinnacle Agricultural Services on July 14, 2011, and commencement of employment with the New York Department of Agriculture and Markets on July 15, 2011, a one-day gap was noted. When questioned regarding this minimal interval, SUBJECT stated that the transition was intentional and that SUBJECT had coordinated the timing to begin the state position immediately upon conclusion of private sector employment. Records obtained from both employers confirmed that SUBJECT's final day of work at Pinnacle was July 14, 2011, and that SUBJECT's first day of employment with the state department was July 15, 2011, consistent with SUBJECT's account.

Similarly, the transition from SUBJECT's state employment to federal employment showed a one-day gap between February 28, 2015, and March 1, 2015. SUBJECT indicated that this brief interval was utilized for administrative purposes and personal preparation for relocation to the Buffalo area. CBP personnel records confirmed SUBJECT's hire date as March 1, 2015. No unexplained unemployment was identified during this period.

SUBJECT's educational timeline was reviewed for continuity with employment history. SUBJECT completed a High School Diploma from Syracuse Central High School, Syracuse, New York, graduating June 1, 2005. SUBJECT subsequently enrolled at State University of New York at Buffalo and completed a Bachelor of Science degree in Agricultural Science, graduating May 15, 2009, with a cumulative grade point average of 3.4. The period from June 1, 2005, to August 1, 2005, represented a two-month interval between high school graduation and college enrollment. When questioned, SUBJECT explained that this gap was used for summer employment and preparation for college relocation. No documentary evidence of employment during this period was required, as SUBJECT indicated the time was primarily spent in personal preparation and summer work of a casual nature.

A review of SUBJECT's employment commenced approximately six weeks following college graduation. SUBJECT graduated from SUNY Buffalo on May 15, 2009, and began employment as a Field Technician at Pinnacle Agricultural Services on June 1, 2009. The two-week interval between graduation and employment commencement was consistent with typical post-graduation transition time. SUBJECT indicated that this period was utilized for final examinations, degree conferral ceremonies, and relocation to Syracuse. No gaps in employment or education were identified that would warrant further investigation or explanation.

The investigator contacted James NMN Rogers, Supervisor, U.S. Customs and Border Protection, Buffalo, New York, by telephone on April 18, 2024, to verify SUBJECT's current employment status and performance. Mr. Rogers confirmed that SUBJECT has been employed as an Agriculture Specialist since March 1, 2015, and remains in that position. Mr. Rogers described SUBJECT's work performance as consistently strong, noting that SUBJECT demonstrates reliability, attention to detail, and sound judgment in agricultural inspection matters. Mr. Rogers stated that SUBJECT maintains regular communication with supervisory staff and adheres to established protocols and procedures.

Mr. Rogers was asked to comment on SUBJECT's attendance and punctuality. Mr. Rogers reported that SUBJECT's attendance record is satisfactory, though he noted that SUBJECT has utilized a moderate amount of sick leave over the past eighteen months, averaging approximately one absence per month. Mr. Rogers indicated this level of absence is within acceptable parameters and did not raise concerns regarding SUBJECT's commitment or reliability. When asked whether SUBJECT has been subject to any disciplinary action, performance improvement plans, or adverse employment actions, Mr. Rogers responded in the negative. Mr. Rogers further stated that SUBJECT has not been involved in any incidents requiring investigation or administrative review.

The investigator inquired regarding SUBJECT's handling of sensitive information, access to restricted agricultural data, and compliance with security protocols. Mr. Rogers confirmed that SUBJECT has access to non-public agricultural inspection records and import documentation. Mr. Rogers stated that SUBJECT has received appropriate training on information security and classified material handling. However, Mr. Rogers noted that during a routine document audit in January 2024, SUBJECT was found to have retained a copy of an inspection report at home rather than storing it exclusively in the secure office filing system. Mr. Rogers indicated that SUBJECT was counseled regarding proper document handling procedures and that the matter was resolved informally without formal disciplinary action. Mr. Rogers emphasized that this was an isolated incident and did not suggest any pattern of security violations or intentional misconduct.

The investigator contacted Maria NMN Stark, former Supervisor, New York Department of Agriculture and Markets, Rochester, New York, by telephone on April 22, 2024, to verify SUBJECT's employment as Agricultural Inspector from July 15, 2011, to February 28, 2015. Ms. Stark confirmed the dates of employment and characterized SUBJECT's performance during this period as competent and professional. Ms. Stark stated that SUBJECT was well-regarded by colleagues and demonstrated strong technical knowledge of agricultural inspection standards and procedures.

Ms. Stark was asked to describe the circumstances of SUBJECT's departure from the New York Department of Agriculture and Markets. Ms. Stark indicated that SUBJECT's separation was voluntary and that SUBJECT had provided appropriate notice prior to accepting a position with the federal government. Ms. Stark confirmed that SUBJECT's final paycheck was processed without issue and that SUBJECT was eligible for rehire. No adverse information regarding SUBJECT's employment conduct or performance was disclosed by Ms. Stark.

The investigator contacted Daniel NMN Banner, former Supervisor, Pinnacle Agricultural Services, Inc., Syracuse, New York, by telephone on April 25, 2024, to verify SUBJECT's employment as Field Technician from June 1, 2009, to July 14, 2011. Mr. Banner confirmed the employment dates and indicated that SUBJECT performed assigned duties in a satisfactory manner. Mr. Banner stated that SUBJECT's departure was voluntary and that SUBJECT had notified the company of intentions to pursue employment in the public sector. Mr. Banner indicated that SUBJECT was in good standing at the time of separation. No derogatory information was reported by Mr. Banner.

spans.title: Unemployment (VIII)
spans.text: The investigator's review of SUBJECT's employment history revealed no periods of unemployment or unexplained gaps requiring further investigation. SUBJECT's transitions between positions were logical and consistent with career progression in the agricultural sector. Educational milestones aligned appropriately with subsequent employment commencement, with minimal intervals explained by standard post-graduation transition periods. All employment dates reported by SUBJECT were verified through direct supervisor contact and documentary records. SUBJECT appeared forthcoming during questioning regarding employment history and provided reasonable explanations for the brief intervals between positions. The one-day gaps between the state and federal positions were consistent with administrative and relocation requirements typical of employment transitions. SUBJECT's current employment with U.S. Customs and Border Protection commenced without delay following separation from state employment, demonstrating continuous professional engagement. No evidence of involuntary unemployment, termination for cause, or extended periods outside the workforce was identified during this investigation.

Mr. Russo stated that he did not know the names of these individuals and could not provide additional identifying information. He reported that he never observed law enforcement activity at the residence and that he had no knowledge of SUBJECT engaging in any illegal activity.

Mr. Russo indicated that he had regular contact (approximately 2-3 times per month) as neighbor from September 2012 to January 2017, consisting of casual conversations and neighborhood interactions. He stated that SUBJECT was generally courteous in these interactions, though he noted that SUBJECT did not appear particularly outgoing or social with neighbors. # Employment (VI)

SUBJECT's current employment was verified with the U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), Agriculture Specialist position, located at 4401 South Park Avenue, Buffalo, New York 14218. According to SUBJECT's personnel records, employment commenced on March 1, 2015, and remains ongoing at the time of this investigation. The position involves inspection and certification of agricultural commodities at the Port of Buffalo.

The investigator contacted the CBP Human Resources office at Buffalo via telephone on March 8, 2024, and spoke with Patricia Chen NMN, HR Specialist. Ms. Chen confirmed SUBJECT's employment status, current salary classification (GS-7), and absence of disciplinary actions or performance issues on record. Official Personnel File (OPF) records were obtained via secure federal records portal and reviewed in full. The OPF contained standard employment documentation including SF-50 forms, performance evaluations for fiscal years 2016 through 2023, and position descriptions. Performance evaluations consistently rated SUBJECT as 'Meets Expectations' or 'Exceeds Expectations' in all evaluation periods.

SUBJECT's direct supervisor, James Rogers NMN, Manager, U.S. Customs and Border Protection, Buffalo, was interviewed by telephone on March 10, 2024. Mr. Rogers reported extensive contact (daily to 3x week) as supervisor from March 2015 to present. Mr. Rogers characterized SUBJECT as reliable, detail-oriented, and knowledgeable in agricultural inspection protocols. He noted that SUBJECT has received two merit step increases during tenure and has been assigned to lead training for new inspection staff. Mr. Rogers reported no concerns regarding SUBJECT's trustworthiness, conduct, or judgment. Mr. Rogers recommends SUBJECT for a position involving national security with the U.S. Government. [March 10, 2024] [CBI01847]

SUBJECT's prior state employment was verified with the New York Department of Agriculture and Markets (NYSDAM), Agricultural Inspector position, located at 50 Wolf Road, Albany, New York 12210. According to SUBJECT's employment records, SUBJECT worked in the Rochester regional office, 317 Commercial Street, Rochester, New York 14604, from July 15, 2011, through February 28, 2015. The position involved field inspection of agricultural facilities and enforcement of state agricultural regulations.

The investigator contacted NYSDAM Human Resources on March 12, 2024, via telephone and spoke with Kenneth Flores MNU, Personnel Records Administrator. Mr. Flores confirmed SUBJECT's employment dates and position classification. Official Personnel File records were requested and obtained via certified mail on March 19, 2024. Records confirmed SUBJECT's employment history and indicated SUBJECT resigned in good standing on February 28, 2015, to accept the CBP position. Performance evaluations on file for 2012 and 2014 indicated satisfactory performance. No disciplinary actions or adverse employment actions were noted in the records.

SUBJECT's former supervisor, Maria Stark NMN, Regional Supervisor (retired), New York Department of Agriculture and Markets, was interviewed by telephone on March 14, 2024. Ms. Stark reported regular contact (3x week to 2x month) as supervisor from July 2011 to February 2015. Ms. Stark described SUBJECT as conscientious and knowledgeable regarding agricultural inspection standards. However, Ms. Stark noted that SUBJECT occasionally experienced financial pressures during the 2013–2014 period and had requested advance payment on vacation time on two occasions due to personal financial constraints. Ms. Stark stated these requests were accommodated through normal payroll procedures and characterized the matter as resolved. Ms. Stark reported no other concerns regarding SUBJECT's conduct or reliability and recommends SUBJECT for a position involving public trust with the U.S. Government. [March 14, 2024] [CBI01851]

SUBJECT's prior private-sector employment was verified with Pinnacle Agricultural Services, Inc., Field Technician position, located at 1847 Erie Boulevard East, Syracuse, New York 13210. According to SUBJECT's employment records, employment was from June 1, 2009, through July 14, 2011. The position involved field testing, soil analysis, and technical support for agricultural clients throughout central New York.

The investigator contacted Pinnacle Agricultural Services, Inc., on March 15, 2024, via telephone and was transferred to the Human Resources department. The investigator spoke with Rebecca Torres NMN, HR Manager. Ms. Torres confirmed that SUBJECT was employed during the stated period and that records were available. Employment verification documentation was requested and received via facsimile on March 16, 2024. Records confirmed SUBJECT's employment dates, position title, and salary information. No disciplinary actions or adverse employment information was contained in the records provided.

SUBJECT's former supervisor, Daniel Banner NMN, Field Operations Manager, Pinnacle Agricultural Services, Inc., was interviewed by telephone on March 17, 2024. Mr. Banner reported regular contact (3x week to 2x month) as direct supervisor from June 2009 to July 2011. Mr. Banner characterized SUBJECT as technically competent and generally reliable in field assignments. Mr. Banner noted that SUBJECT departed the position to pursue state government employment and that the departure was conducted on professional terms. Mr. Banner reported no concerns regarding SUBJECT's honesty or work ethic and recommends SUBJECT for a position involving public trust with the U.S. Government. [March 17, 2024] [CBI01854]

SUBJECT's employment history demonstrates a progressive career in agricultural inspection and regulatory work spanning approximately fifteen years. Employment transitions were logical and professional, with SUBJECT progressing from private-sector field technician work to state government inspection duties, and ultimately to the current federal position. No unexplained employment gaps were identified. SUBJECT has maintained continuous employment since June 2009 with no periods of unemployment exceeding two weeks.

All three employers were successfully contacted and employment records were obtained and verified. Supervisors at all three organizations provided cooperative interviews and characterized SUBJECT as reliable and trustworthy. The single matter of note was Ms. Stark's reference to SUBJECT's temporary financial pressures during 2013–2014, which she characterized as resolved and which did not result in any formal disciplinary action or adverse employment consequences. This matter is addressed separately in Chapter VIII (Financial History).

# Education References (III)

The investigator conducted interviews with academic references familiar with SUBJECT's educational background and character during her undergraduate and secondary education. These references were selected to verify SUBJECT's claimed educational credentials and to assess her academic conduct, reliability, and trustworthiness during her formative years.

Professor David MNU Erikson, Department of Agricultural and Biological Engineering, State University of New York at Buffalo, 237 Farber Hall, Buffalo, NY 14260, was interviewed on March 8, 2024. Professor Erikson reported having extensive contact (2-3 times weekly) as faculty advisor to SUBJECT from August 2007 to May 2009 during her final two years of undergraduate study in Agricultural Science.

Professor Erikson characterized SUBJECT as a conscientious and detail-oriented student who demonstrated strong technical aptitude in soil science and crop management coursework. He noted that SUBJECT maintained consistent attendance and submitted assignments on schedule. He confirmed that SUBJECT completed her Bachelor of Science degree in Agricultural Science in May 2009 with a cumulative grade point average of 3.4. Professor Erikson stated that SUBJECT was organized, asked thoughtful questions during advising sessions, and appeared to take her academic responsibilities seriously. He recalled that SUBJECT worked part-time at the university's experimental farm during her junior and senior years, which he described as evidence of her commitment to the field.

When asked about SUBJECT's character and reliability, Professor Erikson indicated that he had no concerns regarding her honesty or integrity. He stated that SUBJECT was straightforward in her interactions and did not recall any disciplinary issues or academic misconduct allegations. However, Professor Erikson noted that during the final semester of SUBJECT's senior year, she appeared stressed and mentioned difficulty managing her workload due to personal matters, though he did not press for details. He recalled that her academic performance remained solid despite this period, and she completed her degree as planned.

Professor Erikson recommends SUBJECT for a position involving public trust with the U.S. Government. [March 8, 2024] [CBI01847]

Ms. Rachel NMN Kowalski, formerly a classmate of SUBJECT in the Agricultural Science program at SUNY Buffalo, was interviewed on March 15, 2024 at her residence in Ithaca, NY. Ms. Kowalski reported having regular contact (2-3 times monthly) as classmate with SUBJECT from September 2007 through May 2009, during their junior and senior years of undergraduate study. Ms. Kowalski is currently employed as an Agricultural Extension Specialist with Cornell University Cooperative Extension.

Ms. Kowalski described SUBJECT as intelligent, reliable, and well-prepared for examinations and laboratory work. She recalled that SUBJECT was collaborative during group projects and contributed meaningfully to team discussions. Ms. Kowalski stated that SUBJECT was generally organized and maintained a consistent study schedule. She confirmed that both she and SUBJECT graduated in May 2009 and that SUBJECT's academic performance was consistent with the grade point average reported in university records.

Ms. Kowalski noted that during their senior year, SUBJECT occasionally mentioned financial pressures related to tuition and living expenses. Ms. Kowalski recalled that SUBJECT inquired about external scholarship opportunities and part-time employment options in the spring of 2009. Ms. Kowalski stated that SUBJECT did not confide in her regarding specific financial difficulties but appeared somewhat preoccupied during their final semester. Ms. Kowalski further stated that she and SUBJECT have maintained minimal contact (approximately 1-2 times per year) since graduation, primarily through social media interactions and occasional emails.

Regarding character and trustworthiness, Ms. Kowalski stated that she had no concerns regarding SUBJECT's honesty or integrity during their time as classmates. She described SUBJECT as someone who could be relied upon to complete assigned work and meet deadlines. Ms. Kowalski recommends SUBJECT for a position involving public trust with the U.S. Government. [March 15, 2024] [CBI01851]

Mr. Thomas MNU Petersen, retired Academic Counselor, Syracuse Central High School, 3400 Westmoreland Avenue, Syracuse, NY 13210, was interviewed by telephone on March 22, 2024. Mr. Petersen reported having regular contact (approximately 1-2 times monthly) as academic advisor to SUBJECT from September 2001 through June 2005 during her secondary education. Mr. Petersen confirmed that SUBJECT completed her high school diploma requirements and graduated in June 2005.

Mr. Petersen described SUBJECT as a capable student with particular strength in science and mathematics coursework. He stated that SUBJECT maintained satisfactory grades throughout her four years of high school and demonstrated consistent effort in her studies. Mr. Petersen recalled that SUBJECT was generally punctual and compliant with school policies. He noted that SUBJECT participated in the school's agricultural club during her junior and senior years, which he identified as consistent with her later pursuit of Agricultural Science at the university level.

Mr. Petersen indicated that he had no recollection of disciplinary issues or behavioral concerns involving SUBJECT during her time at Syracuse Central High School. He characterized her as well-mannered and respectful toward faculty and peers. When asked about SUBJECT's reliability and character, Mr. Petersen stated that he had no basis to question her honesty or trustworthiness. He recalled that SUBJECT was goal-oriented and expressed clear intentions to pursue higher education in an agricultural field.

Mr. Petersen recommends SUBJECT for a position involving public trust with the U.S. Government. [March 22, 2024] [CBI01854]

# Other Coverage (XVIII)

SUBJECT underwent a previous security clearance investigation conducted by the U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) agency. The investigation was initiated on February 1, 2015, and completed on May 15, 2015. A Secret level clearance was adjudicated and granted as a result of that investigation. Records obtained from CBP confirmed the investigation was conducted in accordance with applicable federal standards and that no disqualifying issues were identified at that time. The investigative file was reviewed for any derogatory information or adverse findings that might have bearing on the current investigation; no such information was located. [May 15, 2015] [CBI02847]

SUBJECT was interviewed regarding the prior clearance investigation and confirmed participation in the CBP background investigation process. SUBJECT stated the investigation covered employment history, references, and financial matters consistent with standard clearance procedures. SUBJECT reported no issues or concerns during that investigation and advised that all information provided was accurate and complete. SUBJECT appeared cooperative and forthcoming during this discussion. [March 18, 2024] [CBI02848]

A comprehensive credit report was obtained for SUBJECT from a major credit reporting agency. The report reflected a credit score within normal range and indicated responsible financial management overall. No active collection accounts, judgments, or liens were identified. The report showed several credit accounts in good standing with consistent payment history. [March 10, 2024] [CBI02849]

However, the credit report did reveal two late payments on a vehicle loan account dating to late 2022 and early 2023. The account showed 30-day delinquencies in November 2022 and January 2023, though the account has since been brought current and no further delinquencies are noted. When questioned regarding these late payments, SUBJECT explained that a temporary reduction in work hours during that period created a cash flow issue, but the matter was resolved once hours returned to normal. Records confirmed SUBJECT's employment was temporarily reduced during that timeframe. No other financial delinquencies or adverse information was identified in the credit report. [March 10, 2024] [CBI02850]

SUBJECT was specifically questioned regarding any foreign travel, foreign contacts, or foreign financial interests. SUBJECT reported no foreign travel within the past ten years and stated that all family members reside within the United States. SUBJECT denied any ongoing contact with foreign nationals or foreign entities and reported no foreign bank accounts, property ownership, or financial interests abroad. [March 18, 2024] [CBI02851]

Passport records were obtained and reviewed. SUBJECT's passport, issued in 2014, showed no entry or exit stamps indicating foreign travel. A second passport was not identified. SUBJECT confirmed the passport information and stated it has not been used for travel. No evidence of unreported foreign travel was identified through available records. [March 15, 2024] [CBI02852]

A comprehensive criminal history check was conducted through the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) National Crime Information Center (NCIC) database, state criminal records repositories, and local law enforcement agencies in jurisdictions where SUBJECT has resided. No criminal arrests, convictions, or pending charges were identified. Court records were reviewed for civil litigation; no judgments or significant civil actions were found on record. [March 12, 2024] [CBI02853]

SUBJECT was questioned regarding any history of substance abuse, including illegal drugs and misuse of prescription medications. SUBJECT denied any history of illegal drug use and reported no prescription medication abuse. SUBJECT acknowledged occasional social alcohol consumption and stated such use has never interfered with work or personal responsibilities. No evidence of substance abuse was identified through the investigation. [March 18, 2024] [CBI02854]

Medical records authorization was requested; SUBJECT signed appropriate release forms. A review of available medical records revealed no significant health issues that would impact SUBJECT's ability to perform duties requiring security clearance access. No mental health treatment, hospitalization, or substance abuse treatment was documented. [March 20, 2024] [CBI02855]

An investigator conducted a neighborhood inquiry at SUBJECT's current residence. Two neighbors were interviewed regarding SUBJECT's character, conduct, and reputation in the community. Both neighbors reported SUBJECT maintains a quiet, orderly residence and is generally unremarkable in neighborhood activities. Neighbors described SUBJECT as a responsible resident who maintains property in good condition and is courteous and respectful in interactions. No adverse information was reported by neighborhood sources. [March 14, 2024] [CBI02856]

Educational credentials were verified through official transcripts and diploma records. SUBJECT's claimed educational background was confirmed through contact with the educational institutions attended. Degrees, dates of attendance, and graduation dates were verified as accurate. No discrepancies between SUBJECT's reported education and official records were identified. [March 16, 2024] [CBI02857]

An investigator conducted a review of publicly available social media accounts and online presence associated with SUBJECT. SUBJECT maintains a limited social media presence with one active account on a major social networking platform. The account contains primarily personal and family-related content with no political extremism, violence, or inappropriate material identified. SUBJECT's online activity reflects personal interests consistent with information provided during interviews. No derogatory, illegal, or security-concerning content was identified. [March 17, 2024] [CBI02858]
